name: Vaṁśī dāsa Bābājī
add: Nandgram Dham: born in 1859 at Majidpur, Jamalpur (Mymensingh); left his wife and young son and settled in Navadvīpa around 1906, in a hut by the river near Bāḍāla ghāṭa, Koladvīpa; an avadhūta bābājī in the general line of Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura. He left this world on the śukla caturthī of Śrāvaṇa, 1944, at Majidpur. Not Gaura Kiśora dāsa Bābājī, who was also called Vaṁśī dāsa before taking the bābājī dress.

name: Śrī Vaṁśīvadana Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: also Vaṁśīdāsa Ṭhākura, Vadanānanda; born c. 1494–1495 in the house of Mādhava dāsa at Kuliyā-grāma (some sources: 1506). He established the worship of the Dhāmeśvara Mahāprabhu Deity at Kuliyā. Sons: Caitanya dāsa and Nityānanda dāsa; his grandson Rāmacandra was adopted as a disciple by Jāhnavā Mātā. Nandgram Dham does not record his disappearance.

name: Vanamālī Ācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: a learned astrologer (jyotiṣī), called «Vanamālī Ghaṭaka», the matchmaker, in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Ādi 15.28–30; Caitanya-maṅgala Ādi 3); he arranged Viśvambhara's first marriage, to Lakṣmīpriyā. Also the brāhmaṇa whom Rukmiṇī sent to Kṛṣṇa. His birth, death and family are not recorded.

name: Vanamālī Vipra (Paṇḍita)
add: Nandgram Dham: «Vanamālī Paṇḍita», the thirty-fifth branch of the Caitanya tree (Ādi 10.73); he came poor from East Bengal to Navadvīpa with his son. He received Kṛṣṇa-prema from the Lord and in a saṅkīrtana in Navadvīpa saw the forests of Vṛndāvana and Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa (Caitanya-maṅgala Madhya 7). Sudāmā, Kṛṣṇa's poor brāhmaṇa friend (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 114). His birth, death, village and his son's name are not recorded.

name: Vāsudeva Datta
add: Nandgram Dham: he prayed to bear the sins of all living beings, and the Lord made a threefold vow over him (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 15). He founded the Madana-gopāla temple at Māmagāchi. His guru is not recorded in any source.

name: Śrī Vāsudeva Ghoṣa
add: Nandgram Dham: born at Kulāi near Kāṭoyā on the Ajaya (some sources: Śrīhaṭṭa); his śrīpāṭa Tamluk is also called Narpota. At the Ratha-yātrā he and Mādhava were the responding singers in Govinda Ghoṣa's party. He wrote Bengali songs about Śrī Caitanya; Nandgram Dham keeps thirty-three. His disappearance is kept on a tithi of Kārtika.

name: Veṅkaṭa Bhaṭṭa
add: Nandgram Dham: of the Vaḍagalai branch of the Śrī (Rāmānuja) sampradāya; both brothers were older than him, Tirumalaya Bhaṭṭa the eldest. The Lord's Cāturmāsya with him was in 1433 Śaka (1511) (Madhya 9.82–165). No source records his disappearance; the family stayed at Śrīraṅgam.

name: Śrī Vidyānidhi
add: Nandgram Dham: this Vidyānidhi is the Mādhva pontiff, not Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi (the start of these notes mixes the two): seventh pontiff of the Uttarādi Maṭha, immediate disciple and successor of Jayatīrtha, who ordained him straight from brahmacarya about a year before his own passing. Born «Kṛṣṇa Bhaṭ» (the maṭha's tradition) or «Nṛsiṁha Śāstrī» (the older Gurucaryā), of a Baḍaganāḍu Karnāṭa brāhmaṇa family. B. N. K. Sharma estimates his pontificate c. 1388–1412. Works: Chāndogya-bhāṣya-ṭīkā (known only indirectly) and Gītā-vivṛti (two manuscripts, Mysore).

name: Vīrabhadra Gosvāmī
add: Nandgram Dham: Vasudhā died early, and Jāhnavā Devī raised him and later initiated him. Chief legacy: the conversion of the neḍā-neḍī ascetics en masse; the founder-figure of the Nityānanda-vaṁśa.

name: Śrīmatī Viṣṇupriyā Devī
add: Nandgram Dham: her father Sanātana Miśra was the rāja-paṇḍita of Navadvīpa; the wedding expenses were paid by Buddhimanta Khān. She was about sixteen when the Lord took sannyāsa at twenty-four, and spent some eighty years in austere bhajana in separation; the Deity of Mahāprabhu she worshipped is still served near Navadvīpa. Bhū-śakti, called jagan-mātā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 47–48).

name: Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: born c. 1626 (sources range from the 1610s to the 1660s); his guru is given as Kṛṣṇacaraṇa Cakravartī of Saidābād or Kṛṣṇacaraṇa's disciple Rādhāramaṇa Cakravartī. Major works: Sārārtha-darśinī, Rāga-vartma-candrikā, Mādhurya-kādambinī, Śrī Gurvaṣṭaka, and an unfinished commentary on the Caitanya-caritāmṛta. He left this world c. 1708, on Vasanta-pañcamī, at Rādhā-kuṇḍa.

name: Śrīla Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura
add: Nandgram Dham: born c. 1507 (1429 Śaka) on the kṛṣṇa dvādaśī of Vaiśākha; his mother Nārāyaṇī Devī was a niece of Śrīvāsa Ṭhākura. He wrote the Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata, first called Caitanya-maṅgala, by tradition in 1535. He left this world c. 1589 (disputed); his samādhi is in the 64 Samādhis area, Vṛndāvana.

name: Śrī Vyāsatīrtha
add: Nandgram Dham: born Yatirāja; in the Mādhva tradition an aṁśa of Prahlāda Mahārāja. Ordained by Brahmaṇya Tīrtha at Abbūr; studied Dvaita for about twelve years under Śrīpādarāja at Mulbagal. Chief disciples: Purandara dāsa, Kanaka dāsa, Vijayendra Tīrtha, Vādirāja Tīrtha and Śrīnivāsa Tīrtha, his successor. He left this world on 8 March 1539 at Vijayanagara, about ninety; his samādhi is at Nava Bṛndāvana, an island in the Tuṅgabhadrā near Anegundi (Hampi).

name: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsadeva
add: Nandgram Dham: also Veda-vyāsa, Bādarāyaṇa; born on a river island at the junction of Dvāpara and Kali (the site is disputed), son of Parāśara and Satyavatī. Nārada told him to compile the Bhāgavatam. He divided the Vedas and compiled the Mahābhārata, the eighteen Purāṇas and the Vedānta-sūtra; his āśrama was Śamyāprāsa on the Sarasvatī. The third ācārya of the Brahma-Madhva-Gauḍīya sampradāya, after Brahmā and Nārada.

name: Yādavācārya Gosvāmī Or Yādava Miśra
add: Nandgram Dham: named in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Ādi 8.67) as a close associate (saṅgī) of Rūpa Gosvāmī in Vṛndāvana; also Yādava Ācārya, Yādava Miśra, Yādavācārya Gosāñi. The Caitanya-caritāmṛta names no formal guru. His birth and death are not recorded.

name: Yadunandana Ācārya
add: Nandgram Dham: his house was east of Raghunātha dāsa's, near Saptagrāma; he also received the mercy of Vāsudeva Datta. The fifth branch of Advaita's tree. He helped Raghunātha dāsa escape to Purī. His birth and death are not recorded.
